0.headline: Digital lending platform Moneyview cuts IPO size; fresh issue halved to Rs 750 crore
0.heading: Digital lending platform Moneyview cuts IPO size; fresh issue halved to Rs 750 crore
0.intro: Moneyview IPO |  investors Crimson Winter, Internet Fund III, Accel, LI Strategic Venture Investment, TI JPNIN India Holdco, and Ribbit Capital have reduced the number of shares offered in the OFS
0.body:
Digital lending platform Moneyview, backed by Accel, Ribbit Capital, Tiger Global Group, and Apis Partners, has decided to reduce the size of its public issue following approval from capital markets regulator SEBI, without refiling its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP).

According to a notice to investors dated September 14, the fresh issue size has been halved to Rs 750 crore from Rs 1,500 crore. Meanwhile, the offer-for-sale (OFS) portion has been reduced to 10.04 crore equity shares from the 13.6 crore shares proposed in the DRHP.

The company filed its draft IPO documents with SEBI in March 2026, and the regulator approved the draft papers in July 2026.

In April 2026, SEBI introduced a rule allowing companies to reduce their fresh issue size by up to 50% without refiling their DRHP. Following the rule change, Moneyview filed an application with SEBI on September 3 seeking approval to reduce the size of its fresh issue.

SEBI approved the application on September 10, following which the company reduced its fresh issue size. The OFS portion was also reduced due to changes in the number of equity shares offered by certain selling shareholders, Moneyview said in its notice.

Under the revised OFS plan, promoters Puneet Agarwal and Sanjay Aggarwal have not changed the number of shares they are offering. However, investors Crimson Winter, Internet Fund III, Accel, NLI Strategic Venture Investment, TI JPNIN India Holdco, and Ribbit Capital have reduced the number of shares offered in the OFS.

Puneet Agarwal's wife, Chitra Agarwal, has also decided to sell 19.35 lakh shares through the OFS, while Apis Partners has withdrawn from the list of selling shareholders.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

Accel is the largest shareholder in Moneyview, with a 21.89 percent stake, followed by Tiger Global Group with a 13.79 percent stake, promoter Sanjay Aggarwal with a 10.33 percent stake, and Ribbit Capital with a 10.2 percent stake.

The objectives of the fresh issue have also been revised. The company plans to utilise Rs 325 crore of the net fresh-issue proceeds to drive growth in loan disbursals under default loss guarantee (DLG) arrangements, while Rs 250 crore will be invested in subsidiary Whizdm Finance to augment its capital base. The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.

Moneyview operates as a digital financial services platform that provides financial products through a network of financial partners. Its platform connects users seeking financial products with banks, NBFCs, insurers, and other financial institutions that offer such products.

Axis Capital, BofA Securities India, IIFL Capital Services, and Kotak Mahindra Capital Company have been appointed as merchant bankers to manage the Moneyview IPO.

In recent months, Hero Motors, Juniper Green Energy, Indo-MIM, Runwal Enterprises, and Rayzon Solar have also reduced their public issue sizes following SEBI's new rule.

1.headline: Hero Motors IPO GMP at 28% ahead of September 16 issue opening; check lot size, timeline and key details
1.heading: Hero Motors IPO GMP at 28% ahead of September 16 issue opening; check lot size, timeline and key details
1.intro: Hero Motors is set to open its initial public offering (IPO) for subscription on September 16, with the issue commanding a grey market premium of nearly 29 percent ahead of the launch.
1.body:
Hero Motors is set to open its initial public offering (IPO) for subscription on September 16, with the issue commanding a grey market premium of nearly 29 percent ahead of the launch.

According to Investorgain, Hero Motors shares are trading at a grey market premium (GMP) of 28.57 percent. Based on the upper end of the IPO price band of Rs 84 per share, the implied listing price stands at around Rs 108, indicating a potential premium of about Rs 24 per share over the issue price.

The Rs 1,000-crore public issue will remain open for subscription until September 18. The price band has been fixed at Rs 79-84 per share, giving the company a valuation of around Rs 3,815.4 crore at the upper end of the band.

Read Also: Who is IKIRU? Indore-based startup behind BRICS gifting order completed in 48 hours

The IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to Rs 600 crore and an offer-for-sale (OFS) of shares worth up to Rs 400 crore. Promoter O P Munjal Holdings will account for Rs 395 crore of the OFS, while Hero Cycles will sell shares worth Rs 5 crore.

Following the issue, O P Munjal Holdings' stake in the company is expected to fall to 49.34 percent from 70.6 percent. Hero Cycles' holding will decline to 1.56 percent from 2 percent.

The anchor portion of the issue will open for a day on September 15 for institutional investors. The share allotment is expected to be completed by September 21, while the company's shares are scheduled to debut on the stock exchanges on September 23.

Hero Motors had filed its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) in June 2025 and subsequently received regulatory approval in September 2025.

The company has since revised the issue structure. The fresh issue has been cut to Rs 600 crore from Rs 800 crore proposed in the DRHP. The OFS composition has also changed, with Bhagyoday Investments withdrawing its proposed sale of shares worth Rs 5 crore. O P Munjal Holdings has raised its OFS size by the same amount to Rs 395 crore from Rs 390 crore earlier.

Investors can place bids for a minimum of 178 shares and in multiples of 178 thereafter. At the upper price band of Rs 84, a retail investor will need to invest at least Rs 14,952 for one lot.

The maximum investment for a retail investor, based on the applicable lot size and limit, would be Rs 1,94,376.

Hero Motors plans to deploy a significant portion of the fresh issue proceeds towards debt repayment and capacity expansion.

The company will use Rs 190 crore to repay debt. Its total outstanding borrowings stood at Rs 289.5 crore as of July 2026.

Another Rs 200 crore from the net proceeds has been earmarked for purchasing equipment for expanding capacity at its manufacturing facility in Gautam Buddha Nagar, Uttar Pradesh.

Check IPO News Here

The balance is proposed to be used for inorganic growth through acquisitions that have not yet been identified and for general corporate purposes.

Hero Motors reported a profit of Rs 43.6 crore for the financial year ended March 2026, marking a 72.9 percent increase from Rs 25.2 crore in the previous year.

Revenue from operations rose 9.06 percent to Rs 1,188.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,089.6 crore in FY25.

Its customer base includes BMW AG, Ducati Motor Holding, Enviolo International Inc, Formula Motorsport, HUMMINGBIRDEV Inc and HWA AG.

ICICI Securities, DAM Capital Advisors and JM Financial are the merchant bankers managing the Hero Motors IPO.

The company operates six manufacturing facilities across India, the United Kingdom and Thailand. It supplies engineered powertrain solutions to automotive original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) across markets including the US, Europe, India and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).

2.headline: Pranav Constructions shares to list tomorrow; GMP signals 36% premium, analysts advise partial profit booking
2.heading: Pranav Constructions shares to list tomorrow; GMP signals 36% premium, analysts advise partial profit booking
2.intro: Shares of Mumbai-based real estate developer Pranav Constructions are expected to make a strong debut on the BSE and NSE on September 15, with grey market trends pointing to a listing premium of more than 35% over the issue price.
2.body:
Shares of Mumbai-based real estate developer Pranav Constructions are expected to make a strong debut on the BSE and NSE on September 15, with grey market trends pointing to a listing premium of more than 35% over the issue price.

The initial public offering (IPO), which was open for subscription from September 7 to September 9, saw exceptionally strong demand across investor categories. The Rs 278-crore issue was subscribed 121 times on the final day of bidding, according to NSE data.

Investors bid for around 271.80 crore equity shares against 2.25 crore shares on offer. Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) led the subscription with 258.71 times demand, while the non-institutional investor (NII) portion was subscribed 208.21 times. The retail portion was subscribed 43.33 times.

Read Also: Who is IKIRU? Indore-based startup behind BRICS gifting order completed in 48 hours

The company had fixed the IPO price band at Rs 118-124 per share. The lot size was 120 shares, meaning retail investors had to invest a minimum of Rs 14,880 at the upper end of the price band.

According to InvestorGain, Pranav Constructions' grey market premium (GMP) stood at Rs 45 per share on September 14. At the upper issue price of Rs 124, this indicated an estimated listing price of Rs 169, translating into a potential gain of 36.29 percent.

Grey market indications, however, are unofficial and can change before the shares begin trading.

The shares are scheduled to list on both the BSE and NSE on September 15.

Market experts remain positive on the company's prospects, particularly given its focus on Mumbai's redevelopment market and its project pipeline. However, they have advised investors who receive allotment to consider booking part of their gains if the stock lists at a substantial premium.

Check IPO News Here

Narendra Solanki, Head-Fundamental Research-Investment Services at Anand Rathi Shares and Stock Brokers, said Pranav Constructions offers pure-play exposure to Mumbai's redevelopment market, with a particularly strong presence in the western suburbs.

As of March 31, 2026, the company had completed 28 redevelopment projects, with 20 projects under construction and another 17 in the upcoming pipeline. The average construction cycle for its projects stands at around 26 months.

Solanki said the company's asset-light model, established presence and execution track record provide it with an advantage in Mumbai's redevelopment market. He also pointed to its growing project pipeline and plans to expand into other regions under the Mumbai Municipal Corporation.

At the upper end of the IPO price band, the company was valued at 19.6 times FY26 price-to-earnings (P/E) and 12.7 times FY26 EV/EBITDA, implying a post-issue market capitalisation of around Rs 13,965 million.

"Given the company's strong market position in the redevelopment segment, asset-light model, execution track record and healthy growth pipeline, we believe the valuation is reasonable considering the growth opportunities in Mumbai's redevelopment market," Solanki said.

He recommended investors who receive an allotment to book partial profits if the stock lists at a premium and hold the remaining shares for the long term.

Mahesh M Ojha, Vice President, Research &amp; Business Development at Kantilal Chhaganlal Securities, said the company's presence in Mumbai's redevelopment market positions it to benefit from a structural opportunity driven by land scarcity and ageing residential societies.

He noted that Pranav Constructions has around 5 million square feet of developable area across its completed, under-construction and upcoming projects.

He also highlighted the company's financial performance, with revenue and profit after tax (PAT) recording a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of around 30% and 34%, respectively, between FY24 and FY26. EBITDA margin improved to 17.2% during the period.

At the upper IPO price band, the stock's post-issue valuation works out to around 19.6 times P/E, which Ojha considers reasonable in view of the company's earnings growth, project pipeline and exposure to Mumbai's redevelopment market.

He recommended that IPO allottees consider booking partial listing gains of 25-30% while retaining the remaining shares for the long term.

"However, investors should monitor post-listing valuation, project execution and cash-flow generation before increasing their exposure," Ojha said.
